headline.purpose: Section titles (h2) — benefits, services, booking, FAQ, reviews.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy; .lead variant (500 weight, 1.125rem) for emphasized intros.

label.purpose: Small uppercase structural labels, e.g. booking modal section headers.

shadows.name: resting-card
shadows.purpose: Default flat-card shadow at rest (benefit/service cards).

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Shadow a card animates to on hover, 350ms ease.

shadows.name: ambient-panel
shadows.purpose: Large soft glow under the FAQ accordion container.

shadows.name: review-card
shadows.purpose: Always-on soft shadow for testimonial cards in the carousel.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Deepest shadow in the system; the booking status modal only.

shadows.name: header-hard
shadows.purpose: Confirmed one-off, solid undiffused shadow on the fixed header only. Do not reuse for new components.

motion.name: hover-transition
motion.purpose: Standard hover transition for buttons, links, and card shadows.

motion.name: aos-fade-up
motion.purpose: Scroll-entrance animation (AOS library) on hero and section titles/cards.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action; gold at rest, swaps to navy on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 10px; font-weight: 700; font-family: 'Montserrat', sans-serif; background-color: #dbbd1a; color: #fff; font-size: 16px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: all 350ms ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: #05172b; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #05172b; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { background-color: #ccc; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Mirrored inverse of the primary button; navy at rest, swaps to gold on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 10px; font-weight: 700; font-family: 'Montserrat', sans-serif; background-color: #05172b; color: #fff; font-size: 16px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: all 350ms ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background-color: #dbbd1a; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #dbbd1a; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Benefit Card
components.description: Centered icon-badge card used in the benefits/trust section; flat at rest, lifts on hover.
components.html:
●

Fully Insured & Secure

All moves are protected and items are handled with the utmost care.
components.css: .ds-card-benefit { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; border-radius: 12px; padding: 24px; background-color: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); transition: box-shadow 350ms ease; text-align: center; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; } .ds-card-benefit:hover { box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); } .ds-card-benefit-icon { width: 70px; height: 70px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 50%; background-color: #dbbd1a33; margin-bottom: 24px; color: #dbbd1a; font-size: 28px; } .ds-card-benefit-title { font-family: 'Montserrat', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; color: #dbbd1a; font-size: 1.125rem; margin: 0; } .ds-card-benefit-desc { max-width: 300px; margin-top: 12px; color: rgb(75 85 99); }

components.name: Service Card
components.description: Image-led card for services; image zooms and shadow lifts together on hover.
components.html:
Residential Moving

Seamless home transitions, handled with care and precision.
components.css: .ds-card-service { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; border-radius: 12px; width: 300px; overflow: hidden; background-color: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); transition: box-shadow 350ms ease; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; } .ds-card-service:hover { box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); } .ds-card-service:hover .ds-card-service-image { transform: scale(1.1); } .ds-card-service-picture { width: 100%; height: 250px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-card-service-image { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; transition: all 350ms ease; } .ds-card-service-content { padding: 24px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 12px; } .ds-card-service-title { font-family: 'Montserrat', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; color: #dbbd1a; font-size: 1.125rem; margin: 0; } .ds-card-service-desc { color: rgb(75 85 99); margin: 0; }

components.name: Booking Input Field
components.description: Dark-theme text field used inside the booking form's navy card — the one place the page departs from its light surfaces.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; color: #fff; } .ds-field-input { width: 100%; height: 40px; border-radius: 10px; appearance: none; background-color: #131314; border: 1px solid #000; color: #fff; padding: 0 12px; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { opacity: 0.5; } .ds-field-input:focus { border: 1px solid #ccc; outline: none; }

components.name: Review Card
components.description: Testimonial carousel card with avatar, star rating, and quote — always-on soft shadow since it lives inside a slider.
components.html:
Jane Smith
★★★★★
Everything arrived in perfect condition. Great service.
components.css: .ds-review-card { background: #fff; border-radius: 16px; padding: 22px; box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.06); display: grid; gap: 14px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; } .ds-review-header { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 56px 1fr; gap: 12px; align-items: center; } .ds-review-avatar { width: 56px; height: 56px; border-radius: 50%; object-fit: cover; } .ds-review-name { font-weight: 700; font-family: 'Montserrat', sans-serif; } .ds-review-stars { color: #fbbc04; } .ds-review-text { color: rgba(0,0,0,.75); margin: 0; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Dashboard-only lead-status pill. Functional, non-brand colors keyed to pipeline stage — intentionally outside the gold/navy palette.
components.css: .ds-chip { padding: 5px 10px; border-radius: 10px; background-color: #e5e7eb; text-transform: uppercase; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; display: inline-block; } .ds-chip--pending { background-color: red; color: #fff; } .ds-chip--in_review { background-color: blue; color: #fff; } .ds-chip--quoted { background-color: aqua; } .ds-chip--closed { background-color: green; color: #fff; } .ds-chip--cancelled { background-color: #ccc; opacity: 0.4; }

narrative.overview:
The system reads moving as a hopeful transition, not a chore — the same optimism as golden-hour light. A single warm gold (Marigold Gold) carries every headline, every primary action, and every moment of confirmation, always against calm neutral ground: white, a soft off-white mist, or one of two deep navies. Nothing else competes for the eye. The voice is warm and reassuring, editorial-clean rather than loud — surfaces sit flat at rest and lift only when touched, copy leans on words like "stress-free" and "handled with care," and the gold never spreads thin enough to feel decorative rather than earned.

The system has two real, confirmed navies rather than one: Midnight Navy, the deeper of the two, grounds structural surfaces (footer, the booking card, the secondary button) and reads as the brand's "night" register. Harbor Blue, a half-step lighter, is reserved for feature moments that need their own atmosphere (the out-of-state banner, the booking section backdrop) — close enough to belong to the same family, distinct enough to signal "this section is a different beat."
keyCharacteristics: One accent color (Marigold Gold) used consistently for headlines, primary actions, hover states, and active indicators — never for large fills.
Two deep navies with distinct roles: Midnight Navy for structure, Harbor Blue for atmospheric feature sections.
Flat-by-default surfaces; shadow appears only as a hover response, always soft and warm-tinted, never hard-edged (with one confirmed exception — see Elevation).
Generously rounded corners (10–18px) throughout; nothing sharp-cornered except the hero's full-bleed image.
Warm, reassuring editorial voice carried in both copy and motion (gentle AOS fade-ups, no aggressive animation).

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Marigold Gold is the only warm color in the system. It marks headings, primary actions, and state changes — never large surface fills. If a new element needs emphasis, reach for gold before reaching for a new color.

rules.name: The Two-Navy Rule
rules.body: Midnight Navy and Harbor Blue are both legitimate, both confirmed, and not interchangeable: Midnight Navy is structure (things that frame the page), Harbor Blue is a feature section's own atmosphere. Don't introduce a third near-navy — pick one of these two.

rules.name: The Gold Headline Rule
rules.body: Every heading (h1–h6) is Marigold Gold by default, set in Montserrat 700. This is a deliberate, site-wide default — don't override heading color per-section without a strong reason; it's the single strongest visual signature of the system.

rules.name: The Hover-Lift Rule
rules.body: Cards are flat at rest and gain a soft, diffuse shadow only on hover (350ms ease). A card that shows its shadow before interaction is off-system.

dos: Do treat Marigold Gold as the system's only accent — for headlines, primary actions, hover states, and active/selected indicators.
Do keep cards and panels flat at rest; only add shadow as a hover response, and keep it soft and warm-tinted.
Do use the primary/secondary button pair as mirrored opposites (gold↔navy swap on hover) rather than inventing a third button treatment.

Do pick Midnight Navy for structural chrome (footer, cards, secondary actions) and Harbor Blue for a feature section's own atmosphere — they are not interchangeable, but both are real, confirmed tokens.
Do keep corners generously rounded (10–18px); a sharp-cornered new component would be off-system.
donts: Don't introduce a new accent color alongside gold — if something needs to stand out, make it gold, larger, or bolder, not a new hue.
Don't copy the header's hard 0 0 10px #000 shadow into new components; it's a confirmed one-off for persistent chrome, not the system's shadow language.
Don't theme new form widgets in the stray purple (#5E17EB) currently leaking from the Google Places autocomplete override — that's a known gap, not an available brand color.
Don't reharmonize the dashboard's functional status-chip colors (red/blue/aqua/green/gray) into gold/navy — they're a distinct, non-brand signaling system for internal staff.
